reference.name: iter10-per-subject
reference.source: autoresearch.trial --name base-per-subject, all three stages, 2026-11-23 (matches experiments/iter10_.../recall.json per-subject rows)
reference.features: iter10 recipe (Gordon+HCP tangent concat + age/sex + L2 logistic C=1e-2), scored per subject: raw decision value cut at 0, no per-group calibration
reference.note: Per-subject scoring: each test subject's label depends only on the training split and its own data, as in the cross-site papers. iter10's per-group calibration used the other test subjects' scores and is no longer allowed (the linter checks this).

rule.note: Two bars on ASD recall, both either-split (one split gains the margin, the other drops at most regress_tolerance), and control recall >= floor on both splits. ACCEPT: +0.3pp vs the current base; the code becomes the new base. OPEN PR: an accepted trial that is also +1pp vs the last PR'd model (iter10-per-subject until the first PR).

screen.rationale: Cheap filter on 6 mixed ABIDE I / II sites. The per-subject base scores ASD recall 0.571 / control recall 0.850 here. 0.54 kills large regressions without requiring a record on six sites; control recall must also stay >= the floor.

loso-site.rationale: Must stay near the base site ASD recall before paying for the institution sweep; control recall above the floor.

loso-institution.rationale: Accept as the new base if site or institution ASD recall gains >= 0.003 vs the current base, the other split drops by at most 0.005, and control recall is >= the floor on both splits. Open a PR only when the accepted trial is also >= 0.01 above the last PR'd model. Always report balanced accuracy, accuracy, AUC and both recalls.

floor.rationale: Control recall must stay >= 60% on every split, so a trial cannot raise ASD recall by calling everyone ASD. 60% is below every cross-site paper's specificity (Heinsfeld 62%, Abraham 72%).
